content:
Update, September 30, 7:37 PM ET: Apple says all issues are now resolved except for Apple TV.

Update, October 1, 8:00 PM ET: Apple says the Apple TV issues are finally resolved.

Apple is currently reporting problems with Apple TV and subscription purchases, and some users are also encountering issues with the company's other services. Details below.

Apple is currently listing 8 ongoing issues

Apple's system status page currently lists Apple TV, the App Store, Apple Fitness+, Apple Music, Apple Music Subscriptions, the Mac App Store, and subscription purchases as experiencing outages or other ongoing issues.

According to Apple, most of the issues began at 4:22 PM ET. Apple lists the App Store, Apple Music, and Mac App Store as undergoing "routine maintenance, which should not impact users," while the Apple TV outage began at 4:43 PM ET, and Apple warned that the service "may be unavailable due to scheduled maintenance."

In our testing, the Apple TV interface failed to load on iOS, but content still loaded and played normally on other devices.

From Neil Windard in the most-read comments

Apple Fitness stopped mid-workout, saying it lost connection with my Apple Watch. I tried to recover it several times and couldn't find the watch, and after restarting the watch it still didn't work, so I gave up.

The outage began shortly after multiple apps — including TestFlight, the App Store, and Fitness+ — started displaying internal localization strings in place of normal interface text. It's not yet clear whether this is related to the other issues Apple's systems are facing.

Downdetector reports further confirm that Apple TV is affected, though reports appear to have peaked and are now declining, suggesting the outage may be tapering off.

We'll keep an eye on things and update this story as soon as there's new information or Apple marks the issues as resolved.

Are you running into problems? Let us know in the comments.
